description: Reaffirm City's leadership in the Homelessness Action Plan 2026.
Endorse performance indicators; report annually, review plan every four years.
Develop comprehensive homelessness data framework with community partners.
Future budget requests for plan implementation will be considered.

chips.text: Recommended
Councillor expressed uncertainty on rental controls and inclusionary zoning due to conflicting data.
A delegate shared personal experience with near-homelessness, thanking Council for their work.
Homelessness rates are high; frontline services are taxed due to shelter closures.
Administration promised to report back on inclusionary zoning

speakers.name: Rob Wilgenhof
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Closure of Prairie Harm Reduction
said: Thanked the fire chief for explaining their robust action plan.
Shared personal experience of nearly being homeless, driving his passion.
Cited high homelessness rates in province, emphasizing urgency.

Represents Meewasin Valley Authority until end of 2026.

chips.text: Recommended

description: Current Board of Revision applicants will not be considered.
City Council will readvertise for Board of Revision vacancies.

chips.text: Recommended

description: Committee recommends appointing Bob Gawdun to Accessibility Committee until 2028.
He would represent the Saskatoon Council on Aging.
Committee also recommends advertising for a citizen vacancy.

chips.text: Recommended
Saskatoon Council on Aging will have a representative.

description: Committee recommends appointing six members to Broadway BID Board.

chips.text: Recommended
Graham Kerr, Jason Robins, Mitchell Ozorio, Casey Loseth, Bijan Arab

description: Committee recommends $2.55 million more for Fire Stations 10 and 11.
New stations will improve west side fire response times.
Funding would come from Major Capital Prioritization Plan.

chips.text: Recommended
Councillor Dubois questioned if smaller fire stations compromise staff comfort.
West side residents would get improved fire service coverage.
Administration promises Fire Station 10 tender by end of summer.

description: BRT stations would move from 25th Street and 5th to 6th Avenue.

chips.text: Recommended
Adjacent property owners and businesses on 25th Street are affected.
South side businesses opposed both 5th and 6th Avenue station locations.

description: Committee recommends new Development Incentives Policy with expanded market housing incentives.

chips.text: Recommended
Councillor Block questioned why the policy returned for approval.
Developers and home builders are affected by new incentives.
Saskatoon & Region Home Builders' Association submitted comments.
City solicitor will prepare necessary consequential amendments for future council consideration.

description: Saskatoon's 2025 financial statements show a $281.6 million surplus.
Overall accumulated surplus strengthened from $5.5 billion to $5.8 billion.
Property tax revenue increased 6.6% due to a 4.96% council hike.
Recommends borrowing $31.7 million for East Side Leisure Centre.
Funds a multi-purpose leisure center facility.

chips.text: Recommended
CFO clarified borrowing covers base facility, not expanded pool lanes.
Saskatoon taxpayers will fund the $31.7 million borrowing.

description: Committee recommends new Saskatoon Transit Bylaw, 2026.
It sets behavior expectations for transit users.
Removes requirement for children under six to have 16-year-old supervision.

chips.text: Recommended
Councillor Jeffries changed his mind, supporting removal of child supervision rule.
Bylaw affects seniors, students, new Canadians, families, and low-income riders.
Where people banned from transit are expected to go was not addressed.
Bus Riders of Saskatoon reported 96% opposition to child supervision rule.
Councillors Dunner and Davies opposed removing the child supervision rule.
Concerns raised about barriers for people experiencing poverty or homelessness.
Administration will launch an education campaign and code of conduct for riders.

description: Recommend loan to TCU Place for a sound system.
City uses existing cash, not third-party borrowing.

chips.text: Recommended
TCU Place receives a fixed-term loan for a new feeder sound system.

description: Saskatoon will study data centre opportunities, risks, and infrastructure demands.

chips.text: Councillor Parker added on-site power and district energy to the study scope.
Taxpayers and neighboring municipalities could be affected by data centre demands.
Data centres raise questions about greenhouse gas emissions and water consumption.
